**Distribution:** All department heads, stage managers, security leads, medical team, and authorised vendors.

---

**1. EVENT OVERVIEW**

The Garden Beats Festival is a two-day outdoor music and arts event held at the Bayfront Event Space, Singapore. The festival features three primary stages, a dedicated wellness and arts pavilion, and a curated food and beverage village. This Operations Plan outlines the schedule, layout, and procedures for the safe and efficient delivery of the event.

**1.1 Key Dates**

*Note: The Garden Beats Festival event_date_start is 2026-03-14 per the Festival Operations Plan. Record status: current. This is a current controlled entry; any change to this date requires written authorisation from the Festival Director and must be circulated as a formal revision.*

**6. Emergency Procedures**

**6.1 General Principles**

In the event of an emergency, the safety of patrons, artists, staff, and vendors takes precedence over all other considerations. The following procedures apply to all personnel on site. All personnel are required to familiarise themselves with the emergency assembly points and evacuation routes prior to the start of their shift. Emergency procedures are reviewed daily at the 07:30 briefing and updated as required in the Ops Log (OP-2026-01-LOG).

**6.2 Emergency Assembly Points**

| Assembly Point | Location | Primary Zones | Secondary Zones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EAP 1 | East Carpark (Zone F) | A, B | C |
| EAP 2 | West Lawn (Zone G) | C, D | E |
| EAP 3 | Festival Green (Zone H) | E, F | D |

In the event of a full site evacuation, all personnel and patrons proceed to the nearest assembly point. Zone Marshals (identified by high-visibility vests with "MARSHAL" printed on the back) direct the flow of movement and account for their zone's staff. Patron assembly is managed by Crowd Management personnel; staff assembly is managed by the Site Operations team.

**6.3 Emergency Response Levels**

The following response levels are used to scale the operational response to an incident. The levels are declared by the Operations Director or, in their absence, the most senior member of the Ops Command Team present on site.

| Level | Definition | Example | Command Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 | Localised incident, no impact on event flow | Minor first aid, small spill | Zone-level response |
| Level 2 | Significant incident, partial impact on event flow | Structural failure, prolonged power outage | Zone E Ops Room |
| Level 3 | Site-wide emergency, event suspension or cancellation | Fire, mass casualty, security threat | Zone E Ops Room / Incident Command Post (ICP) |

**6.4 Activation of the Incident Command Post (ICP)**

The ICP is located at the Main Ops Room (Zone E). Activation occurs automatically upon declaration of Level 2 or Level 3. The ICP is equipped with:

- Dedicated radio channel Ch 0 (emergency traffic only)
- Hardline telephone and mobile backup
- Site maps, zone plans, and utility shut-off locations
- Whiteboards for incident tracking
- Power backup via generator (minimum 4 hours)

The ICP is staffed by the Ops Command Team: Operations Director, Technical Director, Security Lead, Medical Lead, and Logistics Lead. All other personnel are excluded from the ICP unless summoned by the Operations Director.

**6.5 Medical Emergencies**

**6.5.1 First Aid Posts**

| Post | Location | Staffing Hours | Services |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medical Post A | Zone B (near Main Stage) | 10:00 – 23:00 | Full first aid, paramedic on duty |
| Medical Post B | Zone D (near Food Village) | 12:00 – 22:00 | First aid, basic life support |
| Mobile Response Team | Roaming (Zones A–F) | 14:00 – 23:00 | Rapid response, crowd incidents |

**6.5.2 Procedure for Medical Incidents**

1. Any personnel who encounter a medical incident shall call Ch 4 (Medical Lead) and provide: location (zone and landmark), number of casualties, nature of injuries, and any hazards present.
2. Do not move a casualty unless they are in immediate danger.
3. Medical personnel will assess and either treat on site or arrange evacuation to the nearest hospital (Singapore General Hospital, 20 mins by ambulance; Changi General Hospital, 15 mins).
4. All medical incidents, regardless of severity, are logged in the Medical Log (MED-2026-01-LOG) with a timestamp and outcome.
5. For Level 2 or above medical incidents, the Medical Lead briefs the Ops Command Team within 10 minutes of the initial call.

All crowd managers are required to follow the counting and density monitoring procedures below. These procedures are mandatory and will be reviewed at the pre-festival briefing on 17 September 2026.

14.1 Manual Counting Protocol

- Each zone must conduct a manual headcount every 30 minutes during peak hours (1800–2200) and every 60 minutes during non-peak hours.
- Counts must be recorded on the designated counting sheet (Form CM-01) and submitted to the Zone Lead via the radio channel designated for that zone.
- Counts should be conducted from elevated positions where available. If no elevated position is available, two counters must conduct the count independently and cross-check results.
- The following formula is used to estimate crowd size when a full count is not feasible:
  Estimated Crowd = (Number of people in a 10m² sample area) × (Total area in m² ÷ 10)
  Sample areas should be selected to represent average density and should be rotated to avoid bias.
15. STAFF POLICIES AND CODE OF CONDUCT

All personnel listed in this section and in the preceding assignment tables are subject to the
following policies. These policies apply during the festival season (1–30 September 2026),
including all build-up and tear-down days, and at all festival venues and offices.

15.1 General Conduct

- All staff shall treat fellow workers, artists, vendors, and members of the public with respect.
  Harassment, discrimination, or intimidation of any kind is prohibited.
- Staff must wear their issued festival lanyard and identification card at all times while on duty.
  Lost or damaged lanyards must be reported to the HR Office immediately; replacement cost is $15.
- Consumption of alcohol or non-prescribed drugs is prohibited during working hours and while on
  festival grounds, including during breaks.
- Mobile phones may be used for work-related communication only while on duty. Personal calls
  should be limited to break times and taken away from operational areas.
- Staff are expected to arrive at their assigned location at least 15 minutes before their shift
  start time to allow for briefing and handover.

15.2 Attendance and Timekeeping

- All staff must clock in and out using the biometric terminal at the staff entrance (Gate 4) or
  the mobile clock-in app (FestApp) provided by HR.
- Overtime must be approved in advance by the department head. Unapproved overtime will not be
  compensated.
- If a staff member is unable to report for duty, they must notify their department head and the
  HR Office (HR hotline: 6789 0123) at least 2 hours before their shift start time, unless the
  absence is due to a medical emergency.
- Three unexcused absences may result in termination of the staff member's contract.

15.3 Dress Code

- Zone managers and crowd managers: issued yellow safety vest, white polo shirt, dark trousers,
  and closed-toe shoes.
- Technical staff: issued navy coveralls and steel-toe boots. Hard hats must be worn in all
  construction and rigging areas.
- Medical staff: issued white polo shirt with red cross emblem and dark trousers.
- All staff must wear sun protection (hat or cap) during daytime outdoor shifts. Sunglasses are
  permitted but must not obscure identification.

15.4 Grievance Procedure

Any staff member who has a concern or complaint regarding their work, a colleague, or a supervisor
may follow the procedure below:

1. Raise the matter informally with their department head within 7 days of the incident.
2. If the matter is not resolved within 3 working days, the staff member may submit a written
   grievance to the HR Manager, Mrs. Tan Mei Ling, using Form GR-01 (available at the HR Office
   or from the HR hotline).
3. HR will acknowledge receipt of the written grievance within 2 working days and arrange a
   meeting with the staff member within 5 working days.
4. A written decision will be provided within 10 working days of the meeting.
5. If the staff member is dissatisfied with the decision, they may appeal in writing to the
   Festival Director within 7 days of receiving the decision.

No staff member will be penalised for raising a grievance in good faith. Retaliation against a
staff member who has raised a grievance is a serious disciplinary offence.

15.5 Disciplinary Policy

Minor breaches of policy (e.g., lateness, failure to wear lanyard) will result in a verbal
warning. Repeated minor breaches or more serious breaches (e.g., unauthorised absence, failure to
follow safety procedures) will result in a written warning. Gross misconduct (e.g., theft,
violence, falsification of records) will result in immediate termination.
**Personnel Records and Assignments (HR-S03)**

**Section 16: Payroll Information**

16.1 Payroll Schedule

All staff are paid on a monthly basis, with salaries credited to the bank account on file on the
last working day of the month. If the last working day falls on a public holiday, salaries will be
credited on the preceding working day. Advances on salary are not permitted except in cases of
extreme hardship and only with the written approval of the Festival Director.

16.2 Overtime and Time Sheet Submission

- Overtime is payable only when pre-approved by the department head and recorded on the
  official time sheet (Form TS-02).
- Time sheets must be submitted to the HR Office by 12:00 noon on the Monday following the week
  in which the work was performed. Late submissions may result in payment being deferred to the
  next payroll cycle.
- Time sheets must include the staff member's full name, staff ID, date, shift start and end
  times, any break taken, and the total hours claimed. Breaks of 30 minutes or more must be
  deducted from the total hours.
- The Festival Director reserves the right to verify any time sheet against access card records
  or supervisor logs. Discrepancies will be treated as a disciplinary matter under Section 15.5.

16.3 Allowances and Reimbursements

- Meal allowance of $12.00 per shift is payable to all staff for shifts exceeding 8 hours.
- Transport reimbursement for staff using personal vehicles for official errands is claimable at
  $0.80 per kilometre, subject to submission of a route log and receipt for fuel where applicable.
- Claims for out-of-pocket expenses must be submitted within 14 days of the expense being
  incurred, using Form EX-01. Receipts must be attached; claims without receipts will not be
  processed.

16.4 CPF Contributions

For staff who are Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents, CPF contributions will be made in
accordance with the prevailing CPF contribution rates as published by the Central Provident Fund
Board. Contributions will be calculated on the staff member's gross monthly salary, excluding
overtime and reimbursements. Staff who are not Singapore citizens or PRs are not eligible for CPF
contributions and will receive the full salary amount, subject to applicable tax deductions.

**Section 17: Benefits and Leave**

17.1 Annual Leave

- Staff are entitled to 14 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, pro-rated for part-time
  or contract staff based on their contracted working days.
- Annual leave must be applied for using Form AL-01, submitted to the department head at least
  7 days in advance, unless the leave is for an emergency.
- Unused annual leave may be carried forward to the next calendar year, up to a maximum of
  5 days. Carry-forward days must be used by 31 March of the following year.

17.2 Medical Leave and Hospitalisation Leave

- Staff who are unwell must notify their department head and the HR hotline before the start of
  their shift. A medical certificate (MC) from a registered medical practitioner must be
  submitted within 48 hours of the first day of absence.
- Staff are entitled to 14 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Unpaid sick leave may be
  granted at the discretion of the HR Manager in cases where the staff member has exhausted their
  paid entitlement.
- Hospitalisation leave of up to 60 days per calendar year is available for staff who are
  hospitalised, subject to the submission of a hospitalisation certificate from the attending
  physician.

**6. Emergency Procedures**

**6.1 General Principles**

In the event of an emergency, the safety of patrons, artists, staff, and vendors takes precedence over all other considerations. The following procedures apply to all personnel on site. All personnel are required to familiarise themselves with the emergency assembly points and evacuation routes prior to the start of their shift. Emergency procedures are reviewed daily at the 07:30 briefing and updated as required in the Ops Log (OP-2026-01-LOG).

**6.2 Emergency Assembly Points**

| Assembly Point | Location | Primary Zones | Secondary Zones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EAP 1 | East Carpark (Zone F) | A, B | C |
| EAP 2 | West Lawn (Zone G) | C, D | E |
| EAP 3 | Festival Green (Zone H) | E, F | D |

In the event of a full site evacuation, all personnel and patrons proceed to the nearest assembly point. Zone Marshals (identified by high-visibility vests with "MARSHAL" printed on the back) direct the flow of movement and account for their zone's staff. Patron assembly is managed by Crowd Management personnel; staff assembly is managed by the Site Operations team.

**6.3 Emergency Response Levels**

The following response levels are used to scale the operational response to an incident. The levels are declared by the Operations Director or, in their absence, the most senior member of the Ops Command Team present on site.

| Level | Definition | Example | Command Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Level 1 | Localised incident, no impact on event flow | Minor first aid, small spill | Zone-level response |
| Level 2 | Significant incident, partial impact on event flow | Structural failure, prolonged power outage | Zone E Ops Room |
| Level 3 | Site-wide emergency, event suspension or cancellation | Fire, mass casualty, security threat | Zone E Ops Room / Incident Command Post (ICP) |

**6.4 Activation of the Incident Command Post (ICP)**

The ICP is located at the Main Ops Room (Zone E). Activation occurs automatically upon declaration of Level 2 or Level 3. The ICP is equipped with:

- Dedicated radio channel Ch 0 (emergency traffic only)
- Hardline telephone and mobile backup
- Site maps, zone plans, and utility shut-off locations
- Whiteboards for incident tracking
- Power backup via generator (minimum 4 hours)

The ICP is staffed by the Ops Command Team: Operations Director, Technical Director, Security Lead, Medical Lead, and Logistics Lead. All other personnel are excluded from the ICP unless summoned by the Operations Director.

**6.5 Medical Emergencies**

**6.5.1 First Aid Posts**

| Post | Location | Staffing Hours | Services |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medical Post A | Zone B (near Main Stage) | 10:00 – 23:00 | Full first aid, paramedic on duty |
| Medical Post B | Zone D (near Food Village) | 12:00 – 22:00 | First aid, basic life support |
| Mobile Response Team | Roaming (Zones A–F) | 14:00 – 23:00 | Rapid response, crowd incidents |

**6.5.2 Procedure for Medical Incidents**

1. Any personnel who encounter a medical incident shall call Ch 4 (Medical Lead) and provide: location (zone and landmark), number of casualties, nature of injuries, and any hazards present.
2. Do not move a casualty unless they are in immediate danger.
3. Medical personnel will assess and either treat on site or arrange evacuation to the nearest hospital (Singapore General Hospital, 20 mins by ambulance; Changi General Hospital, 15 mins).
4. All medical incidents, regardless of severity, are logged in the Medical Log (MED-2026-01-LOG) with a timestamp and outcome.
5. For Level 2 or above medical incidents, the Medical Lead briefs the Ops Command Team within 10 minutes of the initial call.

14. CROWD COUNTING AND DENSITY MONITORING PROCEDURES

All crowd managers are required to follow the counting and density monitoring procedures below. These procedures are mandatory and will be reviewed at the pre-festival briefing on 17 September 2026.

14.1 Manual Counting Protocol

- Each zone must conduct a manual headcount every 30 minutes during peak hours (1800–2200) and every 60 minutes during non-peak hours.
- Counts must be recorded on the designated counting sheet (Form CM-01) and submitted to the Zone Lead via the radio channel designated for that zone.
- Counts should be conducted from elevated positions where available. If no elevated position is available, two counters must conduct the count independently and cross-check results.
- The following formula is used to estimate crowd size when a full count is not feasible:
  Estimated Crowd = (Number of people in a 10m² sample area) × (Total area in m² ÷ 10)
  Sample areas should be selected to represent average density and should be rotated to avoid bias.

- Mobile phones may be used for work-related communication only while on duty. Personal calls
  should be limited to break times and taken away from operational areas.
- Staff are expected to arrive at their assigned location at least 15 minutes before their shift
  start time to allow for briefing and handover.

15.2 Attendance and Timekeeping

- All staff must clock in and out using the biometric terminal at the staff entrance (Gate 4) or
  the mobile clock-in app (FestApp) provided by HR.
- Overtime must be approved in advance by the department head. Unapproved overtime will not be
  compensated.
- If a staff member is unable to report for duty, they must notify their department head and the
  HR Office (HR hotline: 6789 0123) at least 2 hours before their shift start time, unless the
  absence is due to a medical emergency.
- Three unexcused absences may result in termination of the staff member's contract.

15.3 Dress Code

- Zone managers and crowd managers: issued yellow safety vest, white polo shirt, dark trousers,
  and closed-toe shoes.
- Technical staff: issued navy coveralls and steel-toe boots. Hard hats must be worn in all
  construction and rigging areas.
- Medical staff: issued white polo shirt with red cross emblem and dark trousers.
- All staff must wear sun protection (hat or cap) during daytime outdoor shifts. Sunglasses are
  permitted but must not obscure identification.

15.4 Grievance Procedure

Any staff member who has a concern or complaint regarding their work, a colleague, or a supervisor
may follow the procedure below:

1. Raise the matter informally with their department head within 7 days of the incident.
2. If the matter is not resolved within 3 working days, the staff member may submit a written
   grievance to the HR Manager, Mrs. Tan Mei Ling, using Form GR-01 (available at the HR Office
   or from the HR hotline).
3. HR will acknowledge receipt of the written grievance within 2 working days and arrange a
   meeting with the staff member within 5 working days.
4. A written decision will be provided within 10 working days of the meeting.
5. If the staff member is dissatisfied with the decision, they may appeal in writing to the
   Festival Director within 7 days of receiving the decision.

No staff member will be penalised for raising a grievance in good faith. Retaliation against a
staff member who has raised a grievance is a serious disciplinary offence.

15.5 Disciplinary Policy

Minor breaches of policy (e.g., lateness, failure to wear lanyard) will result in a verbal
warning. Repeated minor breaches or more serious breaches (e.g., unauthorised absence, failure to
follow safety procedures) will result in a written warning. Gross misconduct (e.g., theft,
violence, falsification of records) will result in immediate termination.

**Personnel Records and Assignments (HR-S03)**

**Section 16: Payroll Information**

16.1 Payroll Schedule

All staff are paid on a monthly basis, with salaries credited to the bank account on file on the
last working day of the month. If the last working day falls on a public holiday, salaries will be
credited on the preceding working day. Advances on salary are not permitted except in cases of
extreme hardship and only with the written approval of the Festival Director.

16.2 Overtime and Time Sheet Submission

- Overtime is payable only when pre-approved by the department head and recorded on the
  official time sheet (Form TS-02).
- Time sheets must be submitted to the HR Office by 12:00 noon on the Monday following the week
  in which the work was performed. Late submissions may result in payment being deferred to the
  next payroll cycle.
- Time sheets must include the staff member's full name, staff ID, date, shift start and end
  times, any break taken, and the total hours claimed. Breaks of 30 minutes or more must be
  deducted from the total hours.
- The Festival Director reserves the right to verify any time sheet against access card records
  or supervisor logs. Discrepancies will be treated as a disciplinary matter under Section 15.5.

16.3 Allowances and Reimbursements

- Meal allowance of $12.00 per shift is payable to all staff for shifts exceeding 8 hours.
- Transport reimbursement for staff using personal vehicles for official errands is claimable at
  $0.80 per kilometre, subject to submission of a route log and receipt for fuel where applicable.
- Claims for out-of-pocket expenses must be submitted within 14 days of the expense being
  incurred, using Form EX-01. Receipts must be attached; claims without receipts will not be
  processed.

16.4 CPF Contributions

For staff who are Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents, CPF contributions will be made in
accordance with the prevailing CPF contribution rates as published by the Central Provident Fund
Board. Contributions will be calculated on the staff member's gross monthly salary, excluding
overtime and reimbursements. Staff who are not Singapore citizens or PRs are not eligible for CPF
contributions and will receive the full salary amount, subject to applicable tax deductions.

**Section 17: Benefits and Leave**

17.1 Annual Leave

- Staff are entitled to 14 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, pro-rated for part-time
  or contract staff based on their contracted working days.
- Annual leave must be applied for using Form AL-01, submitted to the department head at least
  7 days in advance, unless the leave is for an emergency.
- Unused annual leave may be carried forward to the next calendar year, up to a maximum of
  5 days. Carry-forward days must be used by 31 March of the following year.

17.2 Medical Leave and Hospitalisation Leave

- Staff who are unwell must notify their department head and the HR hotline before the start of
  their shift. A medical certificate (MC) from a registered medical practitioner must be
  submitted within 48 hours of the first day of absence.
- Staff are entitled to 14 days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Unpaid sick leave may be
  granted at the discretion of the HR Manager in cases where the staff member has exhausted their
  paid entitlement.
- Hospitalisation leave of up to 60 days per calendar year is available for staff who are
  hospitalised, subject to the submission of a hospitalisation certificate from the attending
  physician.
